_comment: Every steward mark found for a through-route in trail_emblems.json, where it was found, and how much of the badge it actually fills (#1543). THIS FILE'S HEADLINE USED TO BE 'NO IMAGE BYTES ARE COMMITTED WITH THIS FILE and that is the point of it', and it is kept here as the thing that changed rather than deleted: the maintainer reversed the opt-in rule on 2026-09-30 and 34 marks are now in the tree at client/src/design-system/assets/trails/. What this file is NOW is the research behind them - the URL each was fetched from, its pixel size, its aspect, and its measured ink at the 18px the badge draws - plus the 31 through-routes that still have no mark and why. 33 of the 36 rows below still read `permission: none asked, none given`, which is not a defect and is the whole point of the opt-out model: nobody has asked these organisations, and pipeline/sources.json's `org_marks.trail_marks` carries the basis and the claim state that lets any of them have theirs out. Corrected 2026-09-30 by review, which found this block still arguing the case for keeping the bytes out while the bytes were in the tree.
_how_to_use_a_row: WHEN A MARK IS ADDED. Fetch `found_at`, put the file in client/src/design-system/assets/trails/, add the row in pipeline/sources.json's `org_marks.trail_marks` with its basis, scope, date and claim_state, and register it in client/src/lib/stewardMarks.ts - in STEWARD_MARKS (keyed by the trail's folded name) and/or STEWARD_MARKS_BY_SLUG (keyed by slug, which is what the BADGE asks). If the badge is to draw it, the slug must ALSO be in map/longTrailNames.ts's SLUGS_WITH_A_STEWARD_MARKER; those two lists disagreeing is how the `cdt` badge drew an empty slot on 267 segments, and stewardMarks.test.ts now checks them against each other. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS FIELD SAID to register it in lib/trails.ts and that 'map/trailBadges.ts needs no change - BADGE_MARK_BY_SOURCE becomes a registry lookup'. That was true before stewardMarks.ts existed and would send a session to the wrong files today: BADGE_MARK_BY_SOURCE still holds exactly two entries and is keyed by SOURCE, not by trail. Corrected 2026-09-30.
_ink_at_18px: MEASURED 2026-09-29. Each mark was letterboxed into an 18-pixel square on #fffdf7 - TRAIL_BADGE_PLATE_DAY's paper - and every one of the 324 pixels scored for WCAG contrast against it. `ink_at_18px` is the share reaching 3:1 or better; `peak_contrast` is the strongest single pixel. The bar is not picked: the A.T. marker already in the tree measures 0.18 ink at 7.4:1, and `clears_the_at` says whether a mark puts at least that much on the plate. A mark below it is not unusable, it is thinner than the one nobody has complained about.
_why_the_thin_ones_are_thin: Almost always because the mark is mostly white, and white on the plate's own paper is nothing. That is a fact about the plate as much as the mark, and it is unresolved: whether a pale mark gets a darker plate is a decision nobody has made. @unvalidated - what would settle it is looking at one on a phone in sunlight, which is #105.

_not_found._comment: The 31 through-routes with no mark here, and what is actually in the way. Grouped because the reasons are not the same and only some are fixable. `_resolved` at the foot is the other direction - a group that emptied and why, kept so the next sweep does not re-derive a blocker that has already been answered.

federally_protected.detail: The last two National Scenic Trails. Markers prescribed in the Federal Register and protected by 18 U.S.C. 701; NPS trail pages serve the arrowhead instead.

found_but_withheld._comment: BOTH MARKS WERE FOUND ON 2026-09-30 AND THE MAINTAINER DECIDED TO LEAVE THEM OUT. Recorded here so the next sweep does not spend the afternoon re-finding them, and so the decision is visible rather than looking like a gap nobody got to. Re-deciding needs written authorisation from the Interior Department, not a better search.
found_but_withheld.why_not_the_pct_answer: The PCT shipped because the Forest Service publishes its emblem and the page carries no restriction. These two are the opposite case and the difference is quoted rather than paraphrased. Both designating notices say: 'Authorization for use of this trail marker is controlled by the administrator of the Trail... whoever manufactures, sells, or possesses this insignia or any colorable imitation thereof... without written authorization from the United States Department of the Interior is subject to the penalty provisions of section 701 of Title 18.' 17 U.S.C. 105 answers copyright and says nothing about that.

pohe.name: Potomac Heritage Trail
pohe.what_it_is: The official trail marker: Capitol dome and bridge in the rounded-triangle shield.

natr.name: Natchez Trace Trail
natr.what_it_is: The official trail marker: a rider on horseback in the matching shield.

no_per_trail_emblem.detail: NPS administers all four and publishes none. johnmuirtrail.org is a fan store whose favicon is a stock photo of a shoe.

blocked_not_absent.detail: coloradotrail.org returns 403 to the page, the JSON API, the favicon and the apple-touch-icon alike. mountainstoseatrail.org challenges every logo request; its favicon slips through and is the stock WordPress logo. NOT ABSENT, AND NOW NOT UNFOUND EITHER - both marks were reached by another route on 2026-09-30 and both were still left out, on ink rather than on access.

colorado-trail.found_at: https://imagecdn.mightycause.com/ - the Colorado Trail Foundation's own logo as it supplies it to its ColoradoGives profile
colorado-trail.why_not: 0.06 against the A.T.'s 0.17 on the same run. It is a combination lockup - a dark-green double-peaked triangle over two lines of type - and most of the square is white margin, so at 18px the type is mush and the symbol is small. A symbol-only crop would clear the bar and is NOT taken here: `permission_meanings.no_modification` is the rule, and cropping somebody's lockup down to the part we prefer is the kind of change that needs asking rather than deciding. The ® on the mark is a second reason to ask.

mst.found_at: https://files.nc.gov/trails/.../MST_Blaze.png - NC Division of Parks and Recreation, the state's own marker rather than the Friends' logo
mst.why_not: 0.02 ink and a peak of 3.6, which is the thinnest thing this file has measured and barely clears the 3:1 the ink share is counted against at all. It is a white disc with a thin black ring and the trail's name curved around it - legible on a signpost, and at 18px a pale circle. Availability was the problem and is solved; legibility is the problem now and is not.

site_compromised.detail: The Pinhoti Trail Alliance domain serves gambling spam - the header image's alt text reads GACOR188. Worth telling somebody. The trail's own mark is a turkey track.

domain_dead_or_photographic.detail: Dead domains, a header baked into a flat photograph, a wordmark tile, or - for the Monadnock-Sunapee Greenway - a landscape illustration measuring 0.02 ink, the thinnest thing tested.

re_fetched_2026_09_30.msg: RE-FETCHED, NOT NEWLY FOUND, and left where it was. The 2026-09-30 sweep returned msgtc.org's logo.png - the same file the 2026-09-29 sweep already had and this group already describes. Measured again: 0.03 ink at 5.3 peak against the A.T.'s 0.17 / 11.0. Recorded so the third sweep does not fetch it a third time and think it has found something.

club_mark_only.detail: The steward publishes a club wordmark and no trail symbol. A club's mark is not the trail's, so these keep an empty slot rather than wear somebody else's badge. Knobstone is the one worth re-reading - see `the_knobstone_question`.
club_mark_only.the_knobstone_question: @unvalidated WHETHER THIS GROUP'S RULE SHOULD HOLD FOR KNOBSTONE. Found 2026-09-30 at https://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/khta-logo.png, 82x150, and it is the only mark this whole sweep returned that CLEARS THE BAR - 0.53 ink at 16.5 peak against the A.T.'s 0.17 / 11.0. An Indiana silhouette with a trail line and a river, over 'KHTA'. WHY IT IS NOT IN `marks` ANYWAY: this is the Knobstone Hiking Trail Association's mark, and trail_orgs.json records the Hoosier Hikers Council as the steward of record - so shipping it would put one body's mark on a trail this repository attributes to another. It is a NARROWER case than the rest of this group, though, because KHTA exists for this trail alone where the Hoosier Hikers Council is a general Indiana club. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: which of the two the trail's badge should name, which is a question about the catalogue rather than about the image, and the maintainer's to answer. The site footer reads '(c) 2026 All Rights Reserved'; nothing was asked and nothing was given, which is true of 33 of the rows that do ship.

no_steward_no_mark.detail: Routes rather than trails: no organisation, and no mark anybody drew. Two of this group - the Grand Enchantment and the Mogollon Rim - turned out to have one after all, which is why the rest were worth checking twice.

_resolved.pct: 2026-09-30. `permission_stated` held one trail and is gone. PCTA's media page still requires written permission for the PCT emblem, the PCT diamond and the PCTA logo, and still nobody has written - what changed is that the mark did not have to come from PCTA. The US Forest Service administers the trail and publishes the emblem on its own page, so the row below is the federal copy under 17 U.S.C. 105. sources.json's `org_marks.trail_marks.pct` carries the basis, including the insignia question that copyright does not answer.

_not_found._the_2026_09_30_sweep: A SECOND SWEEP RAN ON 2026-09-30 after the maintainer said to go and get the rest, and it is recorded per group below rather than summarised, because 'not found' and 'found and not shipped' are different facts and the groups were only carrying the first. SEVEN MARKS CAME BACK AND NONE OF THEM SHIPPED. Two are federal insignia the maintainer decided to leave out (see `federally_protected`). Three measure below the A.T.'s bar by enough that the badge would draw a smudge - the bar is `_ink_at_18px`, and every figure below was measured on the 2026-09-30 re-implementation against that same run's A.T. control of 0.17 ink / 11.0 peak, NOT against the 2026-09-29 column. One is a wordmark, which is the thing the maintainer ruled out twice. One clears the bar and raises a different question, in `club_mark_only`. The sweep's own account of what it could not reach at all is worth keeping too: web.archive.org is blocked from this sandbox, so the dead-domain route is closed here.

marks.name: Pacific Crest Trail
marks.steward: USDA Forest Service (the trail's administering agency); PCTA is the steward org
marks.permission: public domain - a US government work (17 U.S.C. 105), off the agency that administers the trail. Not PCTA's file and not a grant from PCTA, whose own permission requirement is untouched.
marks.measured_with: The `_ink_at_18px` method below, re-implemented on 2026-09-30 rather than re-run from the 2026-09-29 pass. IT DOES NOT REPRODUCE THAT PASS EXACTLY, so read these two numbers against the control rather than against the other rows: the A.T. marker measures 0.18 ink at 7.4:1 in the 2026-09-29 column and 0.17 at 11.0:1 under this implementation. The ink share agrees to 0.01; the peak does not, and nobody has worked out which resampling step moves it. On this implementation the PCT reads 0.23 / 17.5 against that 0.17 / 11.0 control, so `clears_the_at` is true on a like-for-like comparison. @unvalidated whether 0.23 here equals 0.23 in the rows measured on 2026-09-29 - what would settle it is re-running all 36 under one implementation.
marks.aspect_note: THE ONLY ROW WHERE `pixels` AND THE SHIPPED ARTWORK DISAGREE, so read `aspect` here with care. `pixels` is the fetched file, 253x289, which is a page image with white margins; `aspect` 0.875 is that file's. The EMBLEM inside it trims to 206x214, `emblem_aspect` 0.963, and that is what was padded square and resized to the 96x96 in the tree. Measured 2026-09-30 off both files: the shipped ink box is 93x96 at alpha>=64, 0.969, against 0.963 expected - the 0.6% is integer rounding on a 96px raster. A review read the shipped file's full-canvas alpha bbox (which LANCZOS ringing spreads to the edges) against the source's trimmed box and reported a 4.4% horizontal stretch; that comparison was canvas-against-ink and the stretch is not there. Every other row's `pixels` is the fetched file AND its artwork, so this caveat is not needed on them.

_pixels_recheck_2026_09_30: RE-MEASURED FROM THE BYTES when the marks were fetched for the tree on 2026-09-30, and five rows moved. Four were absolute size only, with the aspect unchanged: the three SVGs record viewBox user units rather than rendered pixels (buckeye 121.25x134.03, cumberland 1080x1080, long-trail 322.738x210.842), and Wix served standing-stone at 120x120 rather than the 512x512 first recorded. ONE MOVED IN ASPECT: mason-dixon was recorded 512x512 (1:1) and the file is 300x288 (1.042:1). The `pixels` field for an SVG is user units, which is what `aspect` is computed from and is the only part the badge's fit arithmetic reads.
